required_knowns.claim: Pre-flight verifies the parsed spec, then persists approved state, its spec hash and the captured HEAD baseline.

Explicit post-flight resumes with stored state but parses the current spec and audits it against the saved baseline. A spec-hash mismatch only prints a warning; it neither blocks nor requires renewed pre-flight verification.
The edited contract controls audit scope. Widening touches can remove an UnexpectedFile finding without renewed pre-flight approval. It does not guarantee Held.

Post-flight first persists audit_required and clears previous evidence snapshots. A completed audit attempts to write audit.md and can yield Held, Drift or Broken. Drift/Broken defer release notes and, if history refresh and state persistence succeed, record drift/broken with planner_review. Earlier infrastructure failures can return PostBroken without saving status=broken.

On the would-be Held path, post-flight stability checks cover changes during that phase. A successful Held path can write release/history artifacts. Its saved final state is history_review_required or learned depending on a review bound to the current history snapshot; Held does not itself complete semantic review.
